Class SmcKeyIndex

java.lang.Object
oshi.util.common.platform.mac.SmcKeyIndex
@ThreadSafe public final class SmcKeyIndex extends Object
Connection-independent logic for locating macOS SMC sensor keys by index.

The SMC exposes its keys as a list addressed by index, and returns them in ascending order of the key's four characters. That ordering lets a caller binary-search for a prefix rather than reading every key: on an M2 Max the full index is 2409 keys, of which 297 begin with T and 16 with Tg.

These methods take the index size and a lookup function rather than an SMC connection, so the JNA and FFM backends can share this logic despite their different connection handle types, and so it can be tested without Mac hardware.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_FANS

      public static final int MAX_FANS
      Upper bound on a fan count read from FNum.

      The binding constraint is the key format, not the hardware: String.format("F%dAc", 10) produces the five-character "F10Ac", and reading a key truncates it to four characters, so an eleventh fan would silently read "F10A" instead. Ten is therefore the highest index this naming scheme can express. It also sits above the hardware bound, since no Mac has more than eight fans.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Method Details

    • findKeys

      public static @Nullable List<String> findKeys(int keyCount, IntFunction<@Nullable String> keyAtIndex, String prefix, Predicate<String> mask)
      Locates the keys sharing a prefix, by binary searching the sorted key index and then scanning forward.

      Returns null, rather than an empty list, if the index could not be read reliably. Callers must not cache a null result: an empty list means "this machine has no such keys", while null means "ask again later".

      Parameters:
      keyCount - the number of keys in the index, from the SMC's #KEY key
      keyAtIndex - looks up the key name at an index, returning null if that read fails
      prefix - the key prefix to locate, e.g. "Tg"
      mask - an additional test each candidate key must pass
      Returns:
      the matching keys in index order, or null if the index could not be read

    • reconcileFanKeys

      public static @Nullable List<String> reconcileFanKeys(@Nullable List<String> discovered, long fanCount)
      Reconciles the fan keys found in the key index against the count reported by FNum.

      Discovery is preferred where it produced anything, because the index lists the keys that actually exist. Where it did not, a positive FNum still implies the conventionally named keys, which is what earlier versions of OSHI read directly, so this never reports fewer fans than they did.

      Returns null when the two sources together cannot distinguish "this machine has no fans" from "the keys could not be read", so that the caller does not cache the answer. That happens when discovery failed and FNum read as zero.

      Parameters:
      discovered - the keys found by findKeys(int, IntFunction, String, Predicate), or null if the index could not be read
      fanCount - the count from FNum, or 0 if that read failed
      Returns:
      the keys to read, or null if the answer is not yet known

    • firstPlausible

      public static double firstPlausible(List<String> keys, ToDoubleFunction<String> reader, DoublePredicate isPlausible, String description)
      Returns the first plausible reading among the given keys, in the order given.

      Plausibility is applied here, at read time, for the same reason as in maxPlausible(List, ToDoubleFunction, DoublePredicate): whether a key exists is a property of the hardware and does not change, but whether it currently reports a usable value is not.

      Parameters:
      keys - the keys to read, in preference order
      reader - reads a key and returns the value in its final units, 0 if unavailable
      isPlausible - tests whether a reading is usable
      description - what is being read, for log messages, e.g. "temperature"
      Returns:
      the first plausible reading, or 0 if none were plausible

    • maxPlausible

      public static double maxPlausible(List<String> keys, ToDoubleFunction<String> reader, DoublePredicate isPlausible)
      Returns the highest plausible temperature among the given keys.

      Plausibility is applied here, at read time, rather than when the keys were discovered. Whether a key exists is a property of the hardware and does not change; whether it currently reports a usable value is not, because an idle sensor may report a sentinel below ambient. Filtering at discovery time would let a single unlucky first read cache an empty set and disable the sensor for the lifetime of the JVM.

      Parameters:
      keys - the keys to read
      reader - reads a key, returning the temperature in degrees Celsius
      isPlausible - tests whether a reading is usable
      Returns:
      the highest plausible reading, or 0 if none were plausible
